title: Electromagnetic Waves
source_note: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part I, Reprint 2026-27 (RATIONALISED 2022-23) -- current CBSE syllabus. Equations NOT reliable in this extraction; use board frames as the equation source of truth.
summary:
1. Displacement current id = ε0 dΦE/dt, acts as magnetic field source like conduction current.
2. Accelerating charge → EM waves of same frequency ν. Electric dipole = basic source.
3. Hertz (1887) first produced/detected EM waves in lab, verified Maxwell.
4. E, B oscillate sinusoidally, perpendicular to each other and to propagation direction. E0/B0 = c.
5. c = 1/√(μ0ε0) = speed of light. In medium: v = 1/√(µε).
6. Spectrum: γ-rays, X-rays, UV, visible, IR, microwaves, radio waves (increasing λ, 10⁻¹²m to 10⁶m). Interaction depends on λ and medium.
points_to_ponder:
1. All EM waves travel at same speed in vacuum; differ in wavelength/frequency → different matter interaction.
2. Wavelength correlates with radiating system size: gamma (10⁻¹⁴-10⁻¹⁵m, nucleus), X-ray (heavy atoms), radio (circuits/antennas ~antenna size for efficient radiation). Visible light wavelength >> atomic size though.
3. Infrared vibrates entire atoms/molecules (not just electrons) → heat waves.
4. Human eye sensitivity peak coincides with solar spectrum peak (evolutionary).
exercises:
(8.1-8.10): capacitance/displacement current for charging capacitor; rms conduction current, B amplitude for parallel plate capacitor on ac supply; common quantity for X-ray/red light/radiowave (answer: speed c); E,B direction and wavelength given frequency; radio tuning wavelength band; oscillator frequency→EM wave frequency; E0 from given B0; E0,B0,ω,k,λ,ν from given data; photon energy E=hν across spectrum; wavelength/B-amplitude/energy-density-equality for given E field.

Key terms/glossary: displacement current, conduction current, Ampere-Maxwell law, Maxwell's equations, transverse wave, electromagnetic spectrum, radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays, ozone layer, greenhouse effect.
Named scientists: James Clerk Maxwell, Heinrich Hertz, Jagdish Chandra Bose, Guglielmo Marconi.
